artifacts.caption: Three independently designed HydroSheaf benchmarks and the common evidence taxonomy this paper adds. M3 compares nuclear-tracer/lumped-parameter age inference against the USGS national groundwater-age release; M4 compares reduced-order graph topology against MODPATH particle-tracking connectivity from public MODFLOW archives; M5 compares sparse linear reaction inversion against a 240-scenario live-PHREEQC factorial synthetic benchmark. Each pipeline was locked independently, on its own timetable, before this comparison was constructed.
artifacts.technical_description: Schematic diagram drawn in R (ggplot2 geom_tile/geom_segment) from a declared layout table; not derived from a statistical computation.
artifacts.interpretation: Establishes that the recurring pattern reported in Figures 2-3 is observed across, not designed into, three unrelated benchmark protocols.

artifacts.caption: Benchmark scale and computational cost. Top: scenario counts and total fit counts for M3, M4 and M5, each on its own axis (values differ by roughly two orders of magnitude). Bottom: median per-fit runtime, recorded only for M5.
artifacts.technical_description: Bar charts from benchmark_scale.csv (derive_benchmark_scale.py), which reads scenario/fit counts and runtime directly from each component's own manifest or summary JSON/CSV; no re-simulation.
artifacts.interpretation: The three benchmarks are not comparable in raw scale or in what they record about computational cost; this is disclosed rather than normalised away.

artifacts.caption: Capture-type versus correctness-type metrics under independent, prior-free, uncalibrated evaluation, one panel per component on its own native scale. M4: recall and precision of edge classification against the MODPATH reference (Head-gradient scenario). M3: reportability rate (fraction of fitted rows admitted by the reference-free guard) and within-factor-2 agreement on a held-out cross-validated comparison. M5: recall and precision of active reaction-phase detection, Hydrosheaf Guarded method, against the PHREEQC benchmark.
artifacts.technical_description: Faceted bar chart from headline_metrics.csv (derive_headline_metrics.py); see Table 2 and Methods for the exact source file and averaging convention behind each bar.
artifacts.interpretation: The paper's central cross-component result: in all three physically distinct inference problems, the capture-type axis exceeds the correctness-type axis under independent evaluation.

artifacts.caption: Independent/screening versus calibrated, emulated, or prior-informed evaluation. Left: M3 age log10 R2, held-out uncalibrated versus calibrated emulation (fit on the same folds it is scored against). Centre: M5 Mechanism Resolution Score four-class accuracy, chance level versus a genuine held-out-archetype transfer test. Right: M4 topology, independent F1 versus prior-informed output-graph edge counts (a different metric, plotted on a separate axis).
artifacts.interpretation: Calibrating or conditioning on prior information narrows or removes the capture/correctness gap in Figure 2, but the two calibration exercises shown are not equally rigorous (see rigour_note column and Discussion); neither is independent validation.

artifacts.caption: Within-component detail: every retained benchmark row for M3, M4 and M5, coloured by evidence-taxonomy row type (Table 1), plotted on each component's own headline metric.
artifacts.technical_description: Faceted horizontal bar chart from taxonomy.csv, filtered to rows sharing a common metric within each component panel.
artifacts.interpretation: Shows that negative controls collapse to the floor and informed/prior-informed rows sit above independent rows in every component, which is the internal consistency check behind the Figure 2 comparison.

artifacts.caption: Field- and archive-transfer scope. Top: MODPATH archive endpoint/pathline edge F1 (Savage, Great Miami; Long Island is a documented fallback stub with no active rows). Bottom: median evidence-lifted resolution index (ELRI) for the three field chemistry datasets (Northern Ghana, Talensi, Lower Anayari). No field-transfer benchmark exists for the age layer.
artifacts.technical_description: Faceted horizontal bar chart from field_transfer.csv (derive_field_transfer.py); ELRI medians independently reproduce the values already published in M5's docs/m5_results_summary.md.
artifacts.interpretation: Field/archive transfer scope is uneven across the three layers; none of the three scores shown constitutes field-truth validation (per-component claim ledgers).

artifacts.caption: Common evidence taxonomy applied to every retained benchmark row of M3, M4 and M5.
artifacts.technical_description: Hand-assembled from taxonomy.csv (M4, M5 rows machine-read; M3 scenario labels taken from M3/DECISIONS.md and docs/m3_results_summary.md).
artifacts.interpretation: No row's independence or control-type label contradicts its source component's own claim ledger (DECISION D2).

artifacts.caption: Headline independent/uncalibrated capture-type and correctness-type metrics, all three components.
Screening/independent versus calibrated, emulated, or prior-informed metric, with non-independence stated per row.
Benchmark scale: scenario counts, fit counts, external reference type, and recorded runtime.
Full dataset inventory: every synthetic and field dataset any of the three benchmarks consumes, with source, size, and role.
artifacts.technical_description: Hand-assembled from each component's own manifest/results files and the source_doi/source_url fields already recorded in M4's tier archive summaries; no metadata invented beyond what those files record.
artifacts.interpretation: Gives a reader unfamiliar with M3/M4/M5 the full data basis for the comparison in one place.
